scenes.heading: Integers with powers and brackets
scenes.say: Is negative three squared the same as bracket negative three, squared? One gives nine and the other gives negative nine. Today you will learn to get the sign right every single time.
scenes.caption: Is −3² the same as (−3)²? One gives 9 and the other gives −9. Today you will learn to get the sign right every single time.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Each flip turns the pancake over; two flips and it's back
scenes.science: Each negative factor flips the sign; pairs cancel out
scenes.breaks: Multiplying by −3 flips the sign AND stretches the size by 3, so track the size separately.
scenes.say: Every time you multiply by a negative, the pancake flips. Flip twice and it is right side up; flip three times and it is upside down. The analogy breaks down because multiplying by negative three also stretches the size by three, so keep track of the size separately.

scenes.heading: The bracket decides
scenes.say: With the bracket, you square the whole negative three, and negative times negative is positive nine. Without the bracket, the power comes first, so only the three is squared, then the minus sign makes it negative nine.
scenes.caption: With the bracket, you square the whole −3: (−3) × (−3) = 9. Without the bracket, only the 3 is squared, then the minus sign makes it −9.

scenes.heading: Powers of negatives
scenes.say: An even power of a negative is positive; an odd power stays negative. The square root sign always gives the positive root. But a cube root of a negative is negative, because negative four cubed is negative sixty-four.

scenes.heading: Nested brackets
scenes.question: Work out 5 − [4 − (−3)²] × 2
scenes.say: Peel the brackets like an onion, from the inside out. Negative three squared is nine. Four minus nine is negative five. Times two is negative ten. And five minus negative ten is fifteen.
scenes.caption: Peel the brackets from the inside out. (−3)² = 9. 4 − 9 = −5. −5 × 2 = −10. And 5 − (−10) = 15.

scenes.heading: Substituting a negative
scenes.question: Find 2x² − x³ when x = −3
scenes.say: Put the negative three in brackets before you substitute. Two times negative three squared is two times nine, which is eighteen. Negative three cubed is negative twenty-seven, and subtracting it means adding twenty-seven. The answer is forty-five.
scenes.caption: Put −3 in brackets before you substitute. 2 × (−3)² = 2 × 9 = 18. (−3)³ = −27, and subtracting it means adding 27. The answer is 45.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Even powers hide the minus; odd powers keep it. Bracket negative three squared is nine, but negative three squared without brackets is negative nine. Work nested brackets from the inside out, and always bracket a negative when you substitute it. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Even powers hide the minus; odd powers keep it. (−3)² = 9, but −3² = −9. Work nested brackets from the inside out, and always bracket a negative when you substitute it. Now try the practice questions!
